answer: Decentralized nodes form an interconnected grove of peers, using topological cut verifications to isolate suspicious clusters. A randomly sampled multi-agent auditing committee inspects transaction graphs; if fraud is detected, all colluding identities face automated stake slashing. Because audit committees grow with partition size and collateral requirements compound, the cost to an attacker scales superlinearly. Real-world collateral backed by hard assets like shale reserves or walnut orchard yields cements trust, making large-scale Sybil synthesis economically prohibitive.
